scenario: Eight paintings — Finch, Gallo, Heron, Ibis, Jarvis, Kestrel, Lark, and Merlin — are to be displayed in exactly three gallery rooms: Room 1, Room 2, and Room 3. Room 1 displays three paintings, Room 2 displays three paintings, and Room 3 displays two paintings. The following conditions apply:

rules.description: Finch and Gallo are not displayed in the same room.
Heron and Kestrel are displayed in the same room.
If Finch is displayed in Room 1, then Jarvis is displayed in Room 2.
Lark is not displayed in Room 3.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of paintings to rooms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Room 1: Finch, Gallo, Heron; Room 2: Jarvis, Lark, Merlin; Room 3: Ibis, Kestrel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Room 1: Gallo, Heron, Kestrel; Room 2: Finch, Jarvis, Lark; Room 3: Ibis, Merlin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Room 1: Gallo, Heron, Lark; Room 2: Finch, Jarvis, Kestrel; Room 3: Ibis, Merlin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Room 1: Gallo, Jarvis, Lark; Room 2: Finch, Heron, Merlin; Room 3: Ibis, Kestrel

choices.label: E
choices.text: Room 1: Gallo, Kestrel, Lark; Room 2: Finch, Jarvis, Merlin; Room 3: Heron, Ibis

explanations.correct: Room 1: Gallo, Heron, Kestrel; Room 2: Finch, Jarvis, Lark; Room 3: Ibis, Merlin. Check all rules: Finch (Room 2) ≠ Gallo (Room 1) ✓; Heron (Room 1) = Kestrel (Room 1) ✓; Ibis in Room 3 ✓; Finch is in Room 2 (not Room 1), so the conditional does not fire ✓; Lark in Room 2 (not Room 3) ✓. All rules satisfied.
explanations.A: Finch and Gallo are both in Room 1, violating Rule 1 (they must be in different rooms).
explanations.C: Heron is in Room 1 and Kestrel is in Room 2, violating Rule 2 (they must be in the same room).
explanations.D: Heron is in Room 2 and Kestrel is in Room 3, violating Rule 2 (they must be in the same room).
explanations.E: Heron is in Room 3 and Kestrel is in Room 1, violating Rule 2 (they must be in the same room). Also, Lark is not in Room 3, but Heron is in Room 3 here — the Heron/Kestrel violation is the first disqualifier.

questions.questionStem: If Gallo is displayed in Room 3, which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: When Gallo is in Room 3, Room 3 is full (Ibis and Gallo). Lark cannot go to Room 3 (Rule 5), and Room 3 is already full, so Lark must go to Room 1 or Room 2. Checking all solutions with Gallo in Room 3: Finch can be in Room 1, 2, or 3 (but Room 3 is full, so Room 1 or 2). Reviewing verified solutions with Gallo in Room 3, Lark always ends up in Room 1 or 2 — but specifically Lark is in Room 1 in all of them because Finch, Heron/Kestrel and Jarvis fill Room 2 in varying ways while Lark must be in Room 1 (since Lark can't be in Room 3, and when Room 2 is filled by Heron/Kestrel plus one more, Lark goes to Room 1). In all solutions with Gallo in Room 3, Lark is in Room 1.
explanations.A: Finch can be in Room 1, 2, but not necessarily Room 1 — Finch can also be in Room 2 (e.g., Finch Room 2, Gallo Room 3, Heron Room 1, Ibis Room 3, Jarvis Room 1, Kestrel Room 1, Lark Room 1, Merlin Room 2 is not valid since Room 1 would have 4 members). Finch can be in Room 2 in valid solutions.
explanations.B: Heron (and Kestrel together) can be in Room 1 or Room 2 when Gallo is in Room 3, so this is not necessarily true.
explanations.C: Jarvis can be in Room 1 or Room 2 depending on the arrangement; not forced to Room 2.
explanations.D: Correct — Lark must be in Room 1 in all valid solutions when Gallo is in Room 3.
explanations.E: Merlin can be in Room 1 or Room 2 in valid solutions with Gallo in Room 3; not forced to Room 2.

questions.questionStem: If Heron and Jarvis are both displayed in Room 2, which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: Heron and Jarvis are in Room 2, so Kestrel is also in Room 2 (same room as Heron per Rule 2) — Room 2 is now full (Heron, Jarvis, Kestrel). Ibis is in Room 3. Lark cannot be in Room 3. So Finch, Gallo, Lark, Merlin fill Room 1 (3 spots) and Room 3 (1 remaining spot). Gallo must go to Room 3 (since Room 2 is full and Room 3 needs one more entity alongside Ibis). That means Finch, Lark, Merlin fill Room 1. Merlin in Room 1 is consistent with this — and indeed it must be true that Merlin is in Room 1 in this scenario. So choice E (Merlin in Room 1) could be true (and in fact must be true).
explanations.A: When Heron and Jarvis are in Room 2, Kestrel joins Room 2 (full). The remaining entities Finch, Gallo, Lark, Merlin must fill Room 1 (3 slots) and Room 3 (1 slot, alongside Ibis). Lark cannot be in Room 3, so Gallo must take the Room 3 slot. Finch must then be in Room 1, not able to be in Room 1 per Rule 4's conditional (if Finch in Room 1, Jarvis in Room 2 — Jarvis is already in Room 2, so the conditional is satisfied). Actually Finch CAN be in Room 1 — the conditional is satisfied since Jarvis is already in Room 2. But let's re-examine: Finch in Room 1 is allowed. However, the question asks what COULD be true. Since Finch in Room 1 is actually forced (Finch must be in Room 1 given Gallo is in Room 3 and Lark cannot be in Room 3), choice A must be true rather than merely could be true. But wait — the question asks for 'could be true,' so A also could be true. Re-examining: Gallo must be in Room 3, meaning Finch, Lark, Merlin are in Room 1. A says Finch in Room 1 — this is actually forced. But A is still a correct 'could be true.' The issue is the question stem is 'could be true' and we need exactly one answer. Let me reconsider: Kestrel must be in Room 2 (same group as Heron). So C (Kestrel in Room 1) is impossible.
explanations.B: Room 2 already contains Heron, Jarvis, and Kestrel (three paintings, filling Room 2). Gallo cannot also be in Room 2 — there is no space.
explanations.C: Kestrel must be in the same room as Heron (Rule 2). Since Heron is in Room 2, Kestrel must be in Room 2. Kestrel cannot be in Room 1.
explanations.D: Rule 5 prohibits Lark from being in Room 3.
explanations.E: Correct — with Room 2 full (Heron, Jarvis, Kestrel) and Ibis in Room 3, the remaining entities Finch, Gallo, Lark, Merlin must fill Room 1 (3 slots) and Room 3 (1 slot). Lark cannot go to Room 3, so Gallo takes the Room 3 slot, and Finch, Lark, Merlin all go to Room 1 — including Merlin.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following cannot be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Finch and Jarvis are both displayed in Room 2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gallo and Merlin are both displayed in Room 1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heron and Lark are both displayed in Room 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jarvis and Kestrel are both displayed in Room 2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lark and Merlin are both displayed in Room 3.

explanations.correct: Rule 5 states that Lark is not displayed in Room 3. Therefore Lark and Merlin cannot both be in Room 3 — this is impossible in any valid assignment.
explanations.A: In the verified solution where Finch is in Room 2, Gallo in Room 1, Heron in Room 2, Ibis in Room 3, Jarvis in Room 2, Kestrel in Room 2 — but that puts four paintings in Room 2. Valid solution: Finch Room 2, Gallo Room 1, Heron Room 1, Ibis Room 3, Jarvis Room 2... wait, Heron must be with Kestrel. Finch and Jarvis in Room 2 together: e.g., Finch Room 2, Gallo Room 1, Heron Room 1, Ibis Room 3, Jarvis Room 2, Kestrel Room 1, Lark Room 2, Merlin Room 3 — but that has Lark and Merlin split and Heron/Kestrel together in Room 1. Valid? Room 1: Gallo, Heron, Kestrel (3) ✓; Room 2: Finch, Jarvis, Lark (3) ✓; Room 3: Ibis, Merlin (2) ✓. All rules check out. So A can be true.
explanations.B: Gallo and Merlin in Room 1: e.g., Gallo Room 1, Merlin Room 1 with one more entity (Heron or Kestrel or Jarvis or Lark), and Finch not in Room 1. This is possible in multiple verified solutions.
explanations.C: Heron and Lark in Room 1: Kestrel must also join Room 1 (same group as Heron), giving Room 1 three members: Heron, Kestrel, Lark. This is permitted and appears in verified solutions.
explanations.D: Jarvis and Kestrel in Room 2: Heron must also be in Room 2 (same group as Kestrel). Room 2 would then be Heron, Jarvis, Kestrel — a valid three-member group, consistent with verified solutions.
explanations.E: Correct — Lark cannot be in Room 3 (Rule 5), so Lark and Merlin cannot both be in Room 3.

questions.questionStem: If Finch is displayed in Room 1, which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: Rule 4 states: if Finch is in Room 1, then Jarvis is in Room 2. Since Finch is in Room 1 here (given by the local rule), Jarvis must be in Room 2. This holds in every valid solution under this condition.
explanations.A: Gallo cannot be in the same room as Finch (Rule 1), so Gallo is not in Room 1. Gallo can be in Room 2 or Room 3 — both are possible in valid solutions where Finch is in Room 1. This is not forced.
explanations.B: Heron can be in Room 1 or Room 2 (paired with Kestrel) when Finch is in Room 1. In the solution: Room 1 Finch/Gallo(no)/Heron/Kestrel would overfill; so Heron/Kestrel can be in Room 2 as well. Heron need not be in Room 1.
explanations.C: Correct — Rule 4 directly entails Jarvis must be in Room 2 whenever Finch is in Room 1.
explanations.D: Kestrel travels with Heron (Rule 2). Heron and Kestrel can both be in Room 1 or both in Room 2 when Finch is in Room 1. Kestrel is not forced to Room 2.
explanations.E: Merlin can be in Room 2 or Room 3 in valid solutions where Finch is in Room 1 and Jarvis is in Room 2. For example, Merlin can join Room 2 or Room 3 depending on the placement of the other entities.
